title: Scenario Destroyer
html:
[You have earned 200,000 coins as an achievement reward.]

[Rewards are currently being discussed, with the main contributors as the focus.]

After ‘Izumi,’ Yamata no Orochi’s incarnation, died, the Japanese participants immediately surrendered. Once the [Absolute Throne] collapsed, the power controlling them was completely dispelled, and those who opposed the disasters began emerging from hiding, one after another.

“Thank you. You must be Kim Dokja.”

I recognized his face. Just as I had sought out ‘Asuka Ren,’ Yoo Joonghyuk had also sought out someone among the Japanese participants. I nodded in greeting.

“Kizuki Hiroshi.”

“You know me?”

“You were the one with the hidden scenario for Totsuka-no-tsurugi.”

“Oh, that’s right. Yoo Joonghyuk must have told you.”

Of course, he hadn’t told me anything.

I only knew because I’d read the original novel.

As I remembered it, this man had a constellation sponsor from a later era, connected to the myth of Susanoo and Yamata no Orochi.

“To think you really killed the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’······ You’ve resolved a great many things for us. I will repay this debt.”

Kizuki took charge of the remaining Japanese participants and departed, taking the fallen disasters with him.

He had made good use of the fact that the Japanese participants who had chosen to become disasters wouldn’t die even if their scenario failed.

He wasn’t quite on the level of Izumi, Yamata no Orochi’s incarnation, but Kizuki was also a powerful, intelligent incarnation. He should be able to lead the incarnations for a while even after returning to the Tokyo Dome.

[The constellation of sea and storms, born from a nose, reveals its modifier.]

[The constellation ‘Snake Cutter’ takes a great liking to you.]

The constellation ‘Snake Cutter’ was ‘Susanoo,’ the original owner of the SSS-grade item Totsuka-no-tsurugi.

I glanced at Totsuka-no-tsurugi, which I had returned to Yoo Joonghyuk.

Most of its blade was damaged.

The legend said it had broken while cutting down Yamata no Orochi, so that wasn’t strange.

Just as Yoo Joonghyuk glared at me as if to ask what I was looking at, the companions who had fallen asleep after taking [Ellain Forest’s Vital Force] began waking up, one by one.

“Ah, I really thought I was going to die this time.”

Even after getting up, Lee Jihye held her forehead and shook her head for a long while.

It was probably the shock of hearing Yamata no Orochi’s True Voice directly.

“Seriously, what the hell was that? A few words, and we ended up like that······”

“Even when the commander made a surprise visit while I was a second lieutenant, I didn’t feel like that······”

At the voice from behind him, Lee Hyunsung’s expression immediately froze.

“You seem to be feeling better, Lee Hyunsung.”

“Y-Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi.”

“I told you to follow my group. Why didn’t you listen?”

“Th-that’s······”

Trembling all over, Lee Hyunsung glanced my way.

His face pleaded with me to do something, but there was no way I could help.

Yoo Joonghyuk glared at him for a moment, then turned and walked away.

“Ajusshi.”

I looked beside me and found Shin Yoosung holding on to my collar. She gazed up at me as though seeking comfort, then nestled against my stomach.

I gently patted Shin Yoosung’s back.

“It was hard, wasn’t it? You’ve been through a lot. You held on so well.”

I wanted to say something better, but those were the only words I had.

Shin Yoosung shook her head in my arms.

“Hyung, it wasn’t that hard for me.”

Lee Gilyoung had slipped in before I knew it. He pushed Shin Yoosung aside and climbed into my arms. Despite their bickering, the two children seemed to have grown quite close. Children really did understand other children best. Leaving the two of them together had been worthwhile.

“You’re very popular with the children.”

I looked at the small person who had spoken.

Now, what was his name again? ‘Gillemium,’ perhaps?

“There will be a royal banquet this evening. The inner castle has almost completely collapsed, so it will be a modest affair······ but if you’re willing, we would like to invite you all.”

I looked up into the air.

[Time remaining until the scenario ends: 27 days]

[The disasters have expressed their intention to abandon the scenario. The sixth scenario is therefore scheduled to end early.]

It seemed to be taking a little time because the disasters were scattered everywhere, but once Hiroshi made his way around all of [Peace Land], the scenario would end automatically.

A banquet······

The kind with merrymaking and drinking?

Ah, if that was the case······?

“All right. We’ll attend.”

●

“You seem to be very fond of alcohol.”

“Well······ it’s been hard to come by lately.”

With Gillemium’s help, I brought over a large quantity of the spirits left in the royal castle’s storehouse. The alcohol in [Peace Land] was quite weak, so I needed a lot of it to make the drink I wanted.

[The constellation ‘Snake Cutter’ takes an interest in your brewing method.]

I poured the alcohol into a tub as large as a person, threw in all the ingredients I had, and began stirring.

[The eighth head of the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’]

[The seventh tail of the ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’]

These were parts that had dropped when we defeated Yamata no Orochi. Since it hadn’t been the true body, they were merely fragments rather than actual body parts, but they still contained the power of a Narrative-grade constellation.

Only Yoo Joonghyuk realized what I was trying to do.

“You know about that ‘hidden piece.’”

“You think I’m a Prophet for nothing? Give me your sword.”

Knowing what I intended, Yoo Joonghyuk handed over the sword without protest.

I threw the Totsuka-no-tsurugi he had given me into the alcohol.

This wasn’t how it was normally made, but it was a workaround of sorts.

Rrrrrumble!

Totsuka-no-tsurugi bubbled as it dissolved into the alcohol.

[Two Stories give meaning to your actions.]

[The Stories of the constellations ‘Sovereign of Eight Heads’ and ‘Snake Cutter’ combine.]

[Part of the Story is damaged due to an incorrect retelling.]

It was a shame about the damaged part, but there was nothing I could do.

[The Story ‘Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi’ manifests!]

According to legend, [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi] was a sword that emerged when the drunken Yamata no Orochi’s tail was cut open.

But it could also be obtained through a workaround.

After all, it only needed to be soaked in alcohol.

Lee Jihye asked doubtfully:

“Why are you dropping a sword into that precious booze?”

“Just wait.”

A moment later, a mysterious aura flowed from the entire tub, and a sword radiating pure white light rose through the rippling alcohol.

[The Star Relic ‘Heavenly Sword of Gathering Clouds (天叢雲 剣)’ has appeared!]

There it was, just as expected.

I’m telling you, Ways of Survival never got anything wrong.

Yoo Joonghyuk promptly reached out.

“This is mine.”

“Hey! We killed it together.”

“I was the one who killed it.”

Normally, I would have stubbornly insisted, but this time even Yoo Joonghyuk’s gaze was serious.

This goddamn bastard······

Of course, the Star Relic itself hadn’t been my goal, but having one snatched away right before my eyes still stung.

Just as I reluctantly let go of the sword, unable to fight him here.

[The Star Relic ‘Grass Cutting Sword (草薙 剣)’ has appeared!]

Another sword rose from the tub.

······Huh?

The contents of Ways of Survival raced through my mind.

「Names give birth to Stories, and Stories, in turn, reproduce reality. In the world of the <Star Stream>, [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi] had five names in all. In other words, [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi] was not ‘a single sword.’」

I understood at once.

There were five names passed down for [Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi].

In other words, this sword was one of the other four that had only been mentioned in Ways of Survival and never actually appeared.

I quickly grabbed the sword and said:

“Then this one’s mine. No complaints, right?”

“That’s······”

Yoo Joonghyuk narrowed his eyes and glared at me for a moment before turning away.

“Do as you like.”

I barely managed to let out a sigh of relief.

The sword settled neatly into my hand. Its grip felt satisfying.

The second in the Ame-no-murakumo-no-tsurugi series, the Grass Cutting Sword.

With this sword’s power of dragon slaying (龍殺), I wouldn’t have to fear the dragons I would encounter from now on.

Watching us from nearby, Lee Jihye stuck out her lower lip.

“Honestly, grown men being so petty over a single sword······”

She poked at the tub of alcohol I had brewed and continued playfully.

“If you’re done, can I try some? It smells incredible.”

“You. A minor, and you keep······”

It wasn’t just Lee Jihye.

A crowd had gathered around the tub, its contents rippling gold.

They must all have been badly craving a drink.

Well, just the smell was enough to make you drunk······

“Everyone, help yourselves.”

The moment I gave permission, they began drinking like mad.

“Whoa! How can anything taste like this?”

“It’s heavenly!”

Growing tipsy, they gulped down the golden alcohol, exclaiming again and again. It had been brewed from a constellation’s body parts and fermented with magic power, so of course it tasted good. In fact, drinking it also gave a slight stat increase once you woke up.

“You’re not drinking?”

Wandering nearby, I asked Yoo Joonghyuk. Looking more closely, I saw that, strangely enough, he was making a simple dish.

Grilled skewers of roughly cut meat and vegetables.

Since it was an outdoor party, ingredients brought by the small people were piled up all around us. But ‘Yoo Joonghyuk,’ cooking······

He spoke coldly.

“I don’t eat things made by other people.”

“Why? Afraid they’ll poison it?”

“Because they taste bad.”

“And how good can your cooking possibly be······?”

As I spoke, I quickly took a bite from the skewer Yoo Joonghyuk was making.

But······

Wait, what was this?

Lee Seolhwa, who was helping him nearby, smiled at me and asked:

“It’s good, isn’t it?”

“······Yes.”

It was fucking delicious.

Really, it was delicious.

No, it was the best food I had ever eaten.

How could a meat skewer taste like this?

One corner of Yoo Joonghyuk’s otherwise expressionless mouth had lifted in an infuriating smirk.

Damn it.

Even if he was a regressor, how the hell was this bastard good at cooking, too?

Grumbling to myself, I quietly slipped away. Then I heard what sounded like an instrument playing somewhere.

Very gentle music, with a rich, dignified beauty.

Turning toward the sound, I saw a figure atop the fortress.

The world’s smallest handsome man, whose looks rivaled Yoo Joonghyuk’s.

Kyrgios Rodgraim was there.

He sat on the railing, gazing into the distant sky as he played the viola. Softly, and at times mournfully. A distant, wistful longing. One by one, the people who had been talking boisterously fell silent and listened. The feverish excitement gradually cooled.

First, someone’s eyes reddened.

Then the person beside them burst into tears.

As though it were contagious, before long all the small people began to cry.

People who had missed their chance to cry, too busy running all this way, were finally shedding tears.

The inhabitants of [Peace Land], too, were beings who endured scenarios.

This music was offering comfort to his suffering homeland.

Listening to the melody, I drank a little as well.

I looked beside me and saw that Asuka Ren had approached.

She hadn’t joined the Japanese group.

“Ren-ssi, have you seen Han Sooyoung?”

“Ah. Well, I told her a few details about the setting, and suddenly she said there was somewhere she had to go······”

I see. I’d been wondering why I hadn’t seen her. Had she already gone off to find another hidden piece? Typical of her.

The soft notes of the viola echoed through the shattered fortress, and I looked at Asuka Ren’s flushed face.

Perhaps that was the expression of someone who had reached the end of a long-held dream.

For some reason, I felt I could ask her now.

“How do you feel?”

“······Strange.”

She hesitated for a moment, then continued.

“It made me think I shouldn’t have given up.”

I knew at once what she meant.

Her lips moved for a long time before she wiped away the faint film of tears and asked:

“Do you think anyone imagined a scene like this while reading my manga?”

“I’m certain someone did.”

Asuka Ren smiled sadly and stared down at her hands for a long while.

Her reddened cheeks suggested the alcohol had gone to her head.

“Something else suddenly occurred to me. Perhaps I’m also part of a world someone drew······”

I paused briefly before answering.

“Perhaps this has become a world where that no longer matters.”

“Sorry?”

“Anyway, there was something you started telling me last time······”

Asuka Ren didn’t seem to understand what I meant, so I explained a little. Then she said:

“Ah, right after the serialization ended, I suddenly received an email. Someone wanted to borrow a little of my manga’s setting······”

I was a little startled by this unexpected revelation.

There had been nothing about this in Ways of Survival.

“Borrow the setting?”

“Yes. I didn’t think much of it at the time, so I replied that they could do whatever they wanted. But now that I think about it, all this happened not long afterward······”

“Do you remember any exact details? The email address, for example······”

“The moment I replied, all the related emails suddenly disappeared. So as for the exact address······”

“I see.”

Perhaps something in my voice made her feel bad, because after hesitating, Asuka Ren added:

“······Um, well. I’m not sure, but I think the email address might have started with a t.”

t?

I went blank for an instant, then reflexively asked:

“Was that username······ ‘tls123,’ by any chance?”

tls123.

That was the username of the author of Ways of Survival.

Asuka Ren’s eyes widened as she repeated it.

“Huh? tls123······?”

I urgently pressed her.

“Do you remember?”

“I don’t really remember······ Huh?”

“······What’s wrong?”

After blinking for a moment, Asuka Ren’s eyes had gone blank.

Faint sparks flickered from her body.

“■■■······ ■■”

Huh?

Startled, I asked:

“What did you just say?”

“······Sorry?”

“I mean, what you just said······”

“What do you mean? What did I······?”

Asuka Ren’s face, showing no understanding at all.

A sudden, ominous feeling swept over me.

I immediately activated ‘Character List.’

[Activating the exclusive skill ‘Character List’!]

●

<Character Information>

Name: Asuka Ren

Age: 31

Constellation Sponsor (背後星): Master of Niten Ichiryu

Exclusive Attributes: Creator of Peace Land (Legend), Manga Artist (Rare)

Exclusive Skills: [Kendo Lv.7], [Pen Tip into a Sword Lv.4], [Plausible Footwork Lv.5], [Stimulate Imagination Lv.4]······.

Stigma: [Niten Ichiryu Lv.3]

Overall Stats: [Constitution Lv.55 (Currently Lv.17)], [Strength Lv.55 (Currently Lv.17)], [Agility Lv.49 (Currently Lv.11)], [Magic Power Lv.54 (Currently Lv.16)]

Overall Evaluation: The Overall Evaluation is currently being revised.

●

Just as I had read in Ways of Survival, this woman was undoubtedly the [Creator of Peace Land].

But······

······‘Being revised’?

The next moment, I watched an entire entry in the Attributes Window disappear before my eyes. Like a clump of sand scattering, the letters faded one by one.

●

Exclusive Attribute: Manga Artist (Rare)

●

Very slowly, a chill crept up my spine.

Why had [Creator of Peace Land] suddenly disappeared?

No great constellation could perform a miracle like this.

Tilting her head, Asuka Ren asked:

“I’m sorry, what were we talking about?”

“······We were talking about your work, Ren-ssi.”

“My work?”

Asuka Ren looked as though she remembered nothing.

An expression that suggested she couldn’t recall [Peace Land], or any of the details she had created.

「At that moment, she realized that the world had passed entirely out of her hands.」

My head began to throb.

Had there been a sentence like that in Ways of Survival?

I didn’t know.

But there was one thing I knew for certain.

The viola’s melody ringing through the lonely night.

The small people’s voices singing here and there. This atmosphere, both sorrowful and rich, born of heightened emotions, made me certain of it.

That this very moment was the conclusion of the world called [Peace Land].

There was nothing more to add to this story.

At last, a story had become completely independent of its author.

Thinking of it that way, I suddenly felt I understood why the attribute had disappeared from Asuka Ren.

The moment a world is complete, its author must step down from the position of creator.

A question suddenly occurred to me.

Then where does a story go once it has ended?

[You have come to know the planet ‘Peace Land.’]

[All beings belonging to ‘Peace Land’ faintly sense your gaze.]

[The small constellation of the small planet rejoices in your existence.]

[The beings of ‘Peace Land’ begin writing a legend about you.]

Funny enough, there had been no need to ask.

······So that was it.

Where a story would go after leaving its author had been decided from the very beginning.

Afterward, I asked her a few more questions and even used [Lie Detection]. But she truly remembered nothing.

“I’m sorry, I really don’t know. It does seem like a manga I’ve read······”

To think she felt she had read a story she herself had drawn.

For some reason, it left me feeling melancholy.

Asuka Ren closed her eyes for a moment and pondered something, then continued:

“But I think I enjoyed reading it, too. I’m sure······ I must have.”

Unfortunately, that was where my hard-won lead on the author of Ways of Survival came to an end.

What sort of being the author was, and what they wanted, remained shrouded in mystery.

But I thought I could dimly grasp at least one thing.

Perhaps the author of Ways of Survival had been just as dissatisfied with the original ending as I was.

Perhaps that was why they had given me this ‘text file’ before this world’s end.

If so, I would have to live up to those expectations.

I stepped away from Asuka Ren, who was taking in the scenery, and took out the small ampoule I had tucked inside my clothes.

[Ancient Snake’s Star Blood (星血)]

It was an item I had obtained along with the constellation’s body parts.

At my signal, Lee Hyunsung nodded from a distance and came over.

He hadn’t had anything to drink.

I felt bad, but I had a job for him today.

“Then I’ll leave it to you.”

“You can count on me.”

The job I entrusted to Lee Hyunsung was guarding me.

Because I planned to be unconscious for a while.

When I added [Ancient Snake’s Star Blood] to my cup, the rippling golden alcohol turned the dark red of wine.

[You have drunk alcohol made with ‘Ancient Snake’s Star Blood.’]

[The blessing of the greedy snake tests your mental fortitude.]

This was a hidden piece that even the third-round Yoo Joonghyuk didn’t know about.

A ritual that could only be performed with Orochi’s snake liquor mixed with Star Blood.

Without this, I wouldn’t have given up an attribute as good as ‘King of No Killing.’

[The snake has confirmed your qualification for dragon slaying (龍殺).]

[The new attribute ‘Eight Lives’ prepares to bloom.]

······Done.

The preparations for blooming were complete. Once I slept and woke up, the new attribute should be there.

That took care of one thing. The other was the problem······

I tipped all the remaining alcohol into my mouth, and my head quickly began to spin as intoxication swept over me.

But I couldn’t fall asleep just yet.

I sank to the ground and wrote a message on it.

‘O God of Wine and Ecstasy.’

What was going on? Despite the lively atmosphere, Dionysus gave no response.

Neither did Persephone.

This was a problem.

I had completed the task, but there was no one to take me to the Underworld······

Should I have brought Yoo Sangah after all?

With a direct line to Olympus, I could send a signal right away······

‘O Father of the Rich Night.’

My surroundings went dark the moment I wrote Hades’s modifier.

An eerie chill swept through my entire body.

My vision (視界) spun, accompanied by nausea. When I opened my eyes again, I realized I had already arrived in the Underworld. Only here could the air feel so sinister and unpleasant.

When I looked around, it seemed that, fortunately, I hadn’t fallen into Tartarus again.

Someone stood before me.

[You must not come to the Underworld right now.]

It was neither Hades nor Persephone.

The moment I saw the reaper-like attire, I knew.

“Judge-nim.”

This wasn’t the judge who had guided me last time.

I continued.

“I have come to report that I completed the Queen’s task.”

[I know. I repeat: you cannot enter the palace.]

“······Why?”

[I cannot tell you.]

The judge waved me off as though I were a nuisance.

[Go back. I borrowed the ‘Father’s’ authority to summon you, but you cannot enter.]

“I have an agreement with the Queen. I must go in.”

[Not now. Go back.]

Where the hell did this one get the nerve?

However powerful a judge might be, it was nothing compared to Persephone.

And yet, this one was being so adamant······

“······Are both of them away, by any chance?”

The judge hesitated, then nodded.

[They are.]

“What on earth for······?”

Something important enough for both Hades and Persephone to leave at once.

I couldn’t know for sure, but something major had probably happened somewhere.

It would take at least an emergency meeting of the Twelve Olympians······ But was there anything at this point that would warrant such a summons?

“Did they leave any message for me? Something in case I came to visit······?”

[Who knows? Even if they did, why should I pass it on to the likes of you?]

I knew the judges had different personalities, but I hadn’t expected to get one this prickly.

Still, judging by the way the judge spoke, there did seem to be something.

Someone as meticulous as Persephone wouldn’t simply have left without making arrangements······

Did I have any choice?

“If you help me, I’ll let you have a sip of this.”

What I took from my coat’s inner pocket was some of ‘Yamata no Orochi’s’ snake liquor, which I had brewed in reserve. When I opened the cap, a sweet scent spread through the air, mingled with the mellow fragrance of fermented liquor.

[Th-that is······?]

Even this judge seemed startled.

To beings who had lived for ages, alcohol was like a drug.

The only means of forgetting the tragedies of those long years.

And this was no ordinary alcohol, but snake liquor brewed from a constellation’s body parts. What more needed to be said?

[A-ahem. Ahem······.]

“If you don’t want it, I’ll just leave.”

[W-wait! Very well. I will give you what the Queen left for you.]

······Sure enough, it worked.

This judge was clearly different from the strict one I had met last time.

[Haaa······ Wonderful······.]

After one sip, the tipsy judge smiled as though satisfied, then took a yellow orb from inside their robes and handed it to me.

[Here. Your payment.]

A luminous yellow orb.

I realized it was Shin Yoosung’s soul, which I had so desperately sought.

I took the orb and rubbed it a few times. Giving off a faint light, it floated into the air. I laid my hand on it and conveyed my thoughts.

‘I’m sorry. I took too long, didn’t I?’

The orb gave only a faint cry, as though she had already lost much of her language.

[Ah······ ah.]

A woman who had lost her words and her memories.

Even though she had devoted her entire life to the scenarios, the only story left to her was a history of terrible suffering. Ordinarily, then, someone would tell her this.

You’ve suffered enough. Forget everything now, and rest.

But Shin Yoosung must not rest.

There were still things she had to do in this world.

[A······ jusshi······?]

After struggling for a long time to find her words, the soul trembled.

[Really, truly······.]

‘Yes.’

[Why······?]

‘There’s still something you can do for me in this world.’

I hadn’t come here out of pity for her.

I truly needed Shin Yoosung’s help, nothing more. There was something only she could do, with the high Status of a soul that had accumulated stories over so many years. She answered with a hint of fear.

[What······ do I have to do?]

Keeping my hand on her soul, I showed her some of my thoughts.

After a long silence, Shin Yoosung laughed weakly.

[Haha, ha······ You’re a cruel person, ajusshi······ In a way, even crueler than the captain······.]

‘I’m sorry.’

[But······ all right. I’ll do it. No······ in fact, I really want to do it. It’s what I wanted. This time, I really do want to see this world’s ‘ending,’ too.]

‘You might lose more of your memories. Can you bear that?’

Shin Yoosung nodded.

[I’m not afraid. Because I trust that you······ will tell me the story, ajusshi.]

With those final words, Shin Yoosung’s soul disappeared into the orb.

She probably wouldn’t be able to emerge for a while.

The next time we met would be after she had a body.

The judge, who had been watching us, spoke.

[As you must know, taking a soul out of the Underworld does not resurrect its body. Besides, so much time has already passed for that soul that it cannot settle into a new body.]

The judge gave an unpleasant chuckle.

[If the proper connection arises, reincarnation (還生) may be possible. But that soul has committed too many sins to be born human again. To be born human, it would have to discard all its stories. In that case, it would no longer be the being you knew.]

“I know.”

As Persephone had said, a soul was a story.

So even now, in real time, Shin Yoosung’s soul was becoming ‘something other than Shin Yoosung.’

But surely that wasn’t true of Shin Yoosung alone.

I immediately called my personal representative.

‘Bihyung.’

He said nothing.

I waited for Bihyung to answer, looking down at the orb.

A reincarnation body (還生體) that only a being with high Status could choose······

Having been ruled by stories until now, she would be reborn as a being who ruled over them.

At last, I sensed Bihyung’s presence in the channel. I spoke.

‘I need your help.’

―Help with what?

I didn’t answer.

As Bihyung fell silent with me, I could feel his gaze moving between me and Shin Yoosung’s soul.

He soon understood what I meant.

―D-don’t tell me······ You want me to do ‘that’?

I nodded.

―Hey, think carefully. It’s not as easy as you think. It might be better for her to just fade away here······

‘Want your channel to go under?’

―Damn it. Hey, seriously, I can’t. I’ve never done that before!

‘Then you can start now.’

―Fuck.

After hesitating for a long time, Bihyung finally sent a golden ‘egg’ down from the sky.

An egg descending from the greatest ‘star of stories.’

I placed Shin Yoosung’s soul inside it.

The egg trembled, emitted a vivid radiance, then rose back into the sky.

After a long silence, Bihyung muttered in disbelief.

―To think I’d receive my ‘child’ this way······

My enemies weren’t only inside the scenarios.

Shin Yoosung, who had come from the future of the 41st round.

In this round, she would become a ‘streamer’ for me alone.

The moment my negotiations with Bihyung ended, the judge hurried me along.

[If you are finished, it is time to go back.]

I wondered why the judge was rushing me, then noticed them smacking their lips again and again as they looked at my bottle.

Apparently, the alcohol I had given earlier hadn’t been enough······

Wait a moment.

Come to think of it, hadn’t the judge said Hades and Persephone were away from the Underworld?

“Um, Judge-nim. I have one more favor to ask.”

[I do not know what it is, but this time it would be difficult······.]

“I’ll give you the whole bottle.”

At my words, the judge’s eyes opened wide.

“Please take me to Tartarus once more.”

●

With little time to spare, I went down to Tartarus and quickly came back up. I thought I had only been gone a moment, but in that time the judge had already become completely drunk.

[Then is your business finished?]

“Yes.”

Hades and Persephone’s absence had been a stroke of luck for me. I had only slipped Kim Namwoon a little information, but someone as quick on the uptake as him should be able to make a big difference with that alone.

It made me look forward to the <Gigantomachia> that would come someday.

[The Queen left a message.]

“The Queen did?”

[Yes. I will recite it for you.]

In a deep, solemn voice, the judge relayed Persephone’s words.

[Incarnation Kim Dokja, you have been accomplishing your task in a very interesting way.]

“······”

[Many nebulae of the <Star Stream> are now watching you. And quite a few of them consider you an ominous presence.]
